definitions.explanation: A language used as a shared means of communication between people who speak different native languages or dialects.
The standard form of Japanese based on Tokyo dialect, used across Japan in contrast to regional dialects. Preferred over the older term 標準語 in modern linguistics.

examples.japanese: {英語|えいご}は{国際的|こくさいてき}な{共通語|きょうつうご}だ。
examples.english: English is an international common language.

examples.japanese: ビジネスの{共通語|きょうつうご}として{英語|えいご}が{使|つか}われている。
examples.english: English is used as the common language of business.

examples.japanese: {方言|ほうげん}ではなく{共通語|きょうつうご}で{話|はな}してください。
examples.english: Please speak in standard Japanese, not dialect.

examples.japanese: テレビの{普及|ふきゅう}により{共通語|きょうつうご}が{全国|ぜんこく}に{広|ひろ}まった。
examples.english: Standard Japanese spread nationwide through the spread of television.

examples.japanese: {若|わか}い{世代|せだい}は{共通語|きょうつうご}しか{話|はな}せない{人|ひと}も{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Many people in the younger generation can only speak standard Japanese.

examples.japanese: {共通語|きょうつうご}と{方言|ほうげん}を{使|つか}い{分|わ}ける{人|ひと}は{少|すく}なくない。
examples.english: It is not uncommon for people to switch between standard Japanese and dialect.

notes:
USAGE:
In Japanese linguistics, {共通語|きょうつうご} is preferred over {標準語|ひょうじゅんご} because the latter implies a prescribed standard, while {共通語|きょうつうご} describes the naturally shared common form of the language.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {共通語|きょうつうご}で{話|はな}す (to speak in the common language)
- {共通語|きょうつうご}と{方言|ほうげん} (standard language and dialect)
- {国際|こくさい}{共通語|きょうつうご} (international lingua franca)
